claims.claim: Augustine, Confessions XII.2–5, 7–8 and XI.6, 8–9 are quoted verbatim from E. B. Pusey's translation (1838; Pusey d. 1882), Gutenberg #3296; chapters identified by opening words (Pusey's Gutenberg text has no chapter numbers): XII.2 'The lowliness of my tongue', XII.3 'And now this earth', XII.4 'How then should it be called', XII.5 'So that when thought seeketh', XII.6 'But I, Lord' (cut), XII.7 'But whence had it', XII.8 'But that heaven of heavens'; XI.6 'But how didst Thou speak?', XI.7 'Thou callest us then' (cut), XI.8 'Why, I beseech Thee', XI.9 'In this Beginning'.

Milton, Paradise Lost I.1–26, IX.780–792, IX.1046–1066, IX.1067–1098 verbatim from Gutenberg #20; that file prints the 1667 ten-book text, in which 1674 Book IX is Book VIII; line numbers counted by script from the book heading and match the standard numbering (780, 896, 1046, 1067, 1090, 1098).
'give care' in Paradise Lost IX.1067 is a printing error in this edition for 'give ear'; kept verbatim and explained in the context.

Hesiod (Evelyn-White 1914), Gilgamesh XI (Budge 1920), Huxley 1885 and Darwin 1872 extracts and their commentary are kept from the first version, extracted by the same code; footnote numbers stripped as before.
Tohu elsewhere: Deuteronomy 32:10 (WEB 'waste howling wilderness'); Isaiah 45:18 ('didn't create it a waste'); tohu and bohu together again only in Jeremiah 4:23 (WEB 'waste and void').
Psalm 115:16: Augustine's Latin 'The heaven of heavens are the Lord's'; WEB 'The heavens are Yahweh's heavens'.
Augustine's Latin Bible read Genesis 1:2 'invisible and without form' (Old Latin from the Septuagint aoratos kai akataskeuastos); on day two it called the firmament 'caelum'.
Nicene Creed (381): 'maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible' (wording of the 1662 Book of Common Prayer).
Nachmanides on Genesis 1:1–2 identifies tohu with the Greeks' hyle and bohu with form.
claims.source: Ramban, Commentary on the Torah, Genesis 1:1–2

claims.claim: Rashi on Genesis 1:1: the verse does not teach the order of creation but says 'interpret me' (darsheni).
Origen distinguishes the heaven of Genesis 1:1 from the firmament of day two.
Origen thought it absurd to imagine God planting a garden like a farmer.
John Walton reads Genesis 1 as about functions, with cosmic-temple inauguration and God's rest as taking up residence.
claims.source: Walton, The Lost World of Genesis One (2009)

claims.claim: Matthieu Pageau, The Language of Creation: Cosmic Symbolism in Genesis (2018), reads heaven and earth as poles of unity/identity/purpose and multiplicity/matter, the garden as centre and the fall as movement from centre to periphery.
Jonathan Pageau, Orthodox icon carver, popularises symbolic reading on The Symbolic World podcast.
Jordan Peterson, The Psychological Significance of the Biblical Stories (Toronto, 2017): lecture II 'Genesis 1: Chaos & Order'; lecture IV 'Adam and Eve: Self-Consciousness, Evil, and Death'.

Gordon Wenham, 'Sanctuary Symbolism in the Garden of Eden Story' (1986): God walking (Lev 26:12; 2 Sam 7:6), 'serve and keep' (Num 3:7–8), gold and onyx (Exod 25; 28:9–12), cherubim and eastern entrance, tree of life and lampstand (Exod 25:31–36).

Ezekiel 28:12–16 lament over the king of Tyre: Eden the garden of God; stones; anointed cherub; holy mountain of God; cast out. The stones correspond to the high priest's breastpiece (Exod 28:17–20), all twelve in the Septuagint.
Ezekiel 38:12 'the middle of the earth' is Hebrew tabbur, navel.
Gihon also the Jerusalem spring where Solomon was anointed (1 Kings 1:33–38).
Delphi omphalos called the navel of the world.
Eliade's 'axis mundi'.
claims.source: Mircea Eliade, The Sacred and the Profane (1957; English 1959)

claims.claim: Yggdrasil in the Prose Edda (Gylfaginning), Snorri Sturluson, about 1220.
Tolkien's White Tree of Gondor; Lewis, The Magician's Nephew (1955): Digory fetches an apple from the tree in a walled garden on a hill and is tempted to take one for himself.
Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on Paradise, pictures Paradise as a mountain whose slopes are levels of nearness to God.
claims.source: Ephrem, Hymns on Paradise I–II (tr. Sebastian Brock, 1990)

claims.claim: Augustine held Paradise to be both a real place and a figure.
claims.source: Augustine, The Literal Meaning of Genesis VIII.1

claims.claim: Juris Zarins located Eden near the head of the Persian Gulf.
Tell Fekheriye statue (found 1979) calls itself the ruler's 'image' and 'likeness'.
Peter Lombard, Sentences II.18, on woman taken from Adam's side.
Irenaeus: first humans created as children, to grow; Genesis 3:15 read of Christ.
Sartre on shame and the look.
East as direction of exile: Genesis 3:24; 4:16; 11:2; 13:11.
Original sin table (Trent, Catechism 396–409, Augsburg II, Westminster 6, Orthodox ancestral sin, Jewish view).
claims.source: Kept from first version; sources as there

claims.claim: Nod means 'wandering'; 'keeper' (4:9) and 'keep' (2:15) are both shamar.
Flood as un-creation: 7:11 and 8:2 reverse 1:6–9; ruach 1:2 and 8:1; blessing 9:1 echoes 1:28.
George Smith's discovery (read 3 December 1872), Woolley at Ur (1929), Shuruppak deposits c. 2900 BC, geological consensus.
claims.source: Kept from first version; sources as there

claims.claim: Copernicus 1543; Galileo Sidereus Nuncius 1610, phases of Venus late 1610, condemnation 1633.

Danielson: in medieval cosmology the centre was the lowest place; Galileo in Sidereus Nuncius says he will show the earth is a wandering body and not the sump of the universe's dregs; the 'demotion' story is later.
claims.source: Dennis R. Danielson, 'The Great Copernican Cliché', American Journal of Physics 69 (2001), 1029–1035

claims.claim: Ptolemy: earth like a point relative to the heavens; Boethius the same.
claims.source: Almagest I.6; Consolation of Philosophy II, prose 7

claims.claim: Dante places Satan at the earth's centre.
Freud's three blows (cosmological, biological, psychological), 1917.
claims.source: 'A Difficulty in the Path of Psycho-Analysis' (1917); Introductory Lectures, lecture 18

claims.claim: Weber's 'disenchantment of the world'.
claims.source: 'Science as a Vocation', lecture delivered 1917, published 1919

claims.claim: Voyager 1 'pale blue dot' photograph, 14 February 1990, about 6 billion km; Sagan's book 1994.
Etemenanki 'house of the foundation of heaven and earth'; Herodotus' eight towers.
Bab-ili 'gate of god'; Hebrew balal 'confuse'.
John 1:1 en archē = Septuagint Genesis 1:1; eskēnōsen 'pitched his tent' (John 1:14).
Heraclitus on logos; Stoic logos; Philo's logos as God's instrument in creation.
claims.source: Heraclitus DK 22 B1–2; Philo, On the Creation of the World; Dodd 1953

claims.claim: John 1:51 recalls Jacob's ladder (Genesis 28:12).
Haydn's Creation opens with 'The Representation of Chaos' and bursts into C major at 'and there was light'.
Bruckner's Locus iste (1869) for the consecration of the votive chapel in Linz Cathedral.
